service.name: Wedding cocktail hour music
service.serviceType: Live music for wedding cocktail hours
service.description: Jazz duo, acoustic duo and solo guitarist bookings for wedding cocktail hours across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor, at published rates.

faqs.q: Is cocktail hour music necessary at a wedding?
faqs.a: Yes, and it earns its line. The ceremony has ended, the couple is away for photographs, and the guests are deciding what kind of night this is. Live music carries that turn. A duo at conversation volume holds the hour without competing with the conversations it exists to start.

faqs.q: What music should play during a wedding cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Jazz standards and singer-songwriter covers, at conversation volume. The repertoire matters less than the level: 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table lets two strangers introduce themselves without leaning in. Upright bass and guitar is the instrumentation built for exactly that.

faqs.q: How long is a wedding cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Sixty minutes is standard. It stretches to 90 when the venue turns one space from ceremony to reception, because guests cannot go back in until the flip is done. Added time bills at the same hourly rate in 30-minute increments; there is no overtime rate.

faqs.q: Should we book a band or a DJ for cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Two players, for this hour. A duo reads the crowd, takes a request, and lands at a volume people can talk across. A DJ earns its fee later, carrying the dance floor after dinner. Both sit on the same published rate card, so the comparison costs nothing to make.

faqs.q: Can one booking cover the cocktail hour and dinner?
faqs.a: Yes. The same two players carry cocktails and dinner on one line of the contract, with sound included and a published range covering the whole block. One load-in, one sound check, one invoice, and the hour never goes silent between sets.
